dan: Quick heads-up: vendor scheduled PDU handshake in eu-west3 rack P2 on Tue 2026-04-12 02:00-04:00 UTC. We plan staggered PDU cycles across the rack to eliminate a latent PDU firmware bug. Expected: transient NIC flaps, some GPU host reboots, possible short-lived RPC retries. Aim to keep infra invisible to customers but prepare for retries and alerting.

eva: Acknowledged. Which specific hosts and any pinned Dedicated tenants we need to call out?

dan: Hosts: host-011..host-018 (8 hosts). Affected pool: eu-west3-gpu-pool-b. Dedicated pinned: tenant-dedicated-7 on host-014 and host-017. We'll try live-migration off those hosts; if LM fails we will drain and failover to reserve nodes.

mike: Kicking off a live-migrate capability probe now: `./tools/check-lm.sh eu-west3-gpu-pool-b --summary`. Will paste output here in 15m.

sophie: If we failover to cross-region warm nodes (eu-west2 or us-east1), note cost delta. Rough calc: +25% serving spend during the 2h window for impacted routes. @natalie can you confirm if we have a burn cap for such bursts? :moneybag:

alex: Proposed ops sequence (short):
1) set maintenance flag on hosts: `rctl maintenance set --hosts host-011..host-018 --reason "vendor PDU handshake"`
2) pre-warm 4 spares in eu-west2: `infractl node spinup --region eu-west2 --count 4 --flavor g4dn`
3) run LM probe; if any host fails LM -> mark for manual drain
4) power-cycle hosts sequentially with 10m gap: `for h in {011..018}; do infractl drain $h --grace 120 && vendorctl pdu-cycle $h && sleep 600; done`
5) monitor route-level 95p latency and 5xx rate; auto-escalate at 2x 5xx baseline for >5m

maintenance-bot: INFRA-1298 created; ops calendar entry set; automated update message scheduled to #customer-success.

dan: Action items: eva prepare host->tenant export and opt-out list (customers with hard SLAs); mike post LM probe results ASAP; alex coordinate pre-warm and autoscale min bump; natalie validate budget for cross-region burst; I'll draft the Dedicated customer comms. SRE-oncall: stand by during the window for rapid rollback.

eva: Host->tenant mapping uploaded to thread. Opt-outs: tenant-secure-2 (compliance) and tenant-finance-1 flagged; we'll exclude them unless they explicitly opt-in.

mike: LM probe results (summary): 7/8 hosts successfully accept live migration. host-014 shows driver/kernel handshake failure in our probe (stack trace snippet: "nvml: driver mismatch"). Recommendation: exclude host-014 from LM automation; plan manual patch/reboot post-maintenance. Full probe log attached to ticket.

dan: Good find. We'll exclude host-014 from LM automation and plan to manually patch it after the PDU cycles. Updating runbook and ops calendar.

sophie: FYI ops: if we see RPC timeouts to the embedding route, consider temporarily routing that route to eu-west2 warm standby to preserve SLA for core customers. That will increase cost but keeps latency consistent.

alex: Noted. I'll set autoscaler min=2 for eu-west3-gpu-pool-b during maintenance to ensure headroom and reduce scheduling churn. Command: `autoscalectl set-min --pool eu-west3-gpu-pool-b --min 2 --until 2026-04-12T05:00:00Z`

natalie: Budget check: we have a 30k/month burst buffer; this operation fits within emergency burst allocation. I'll include a post-mortem cost line item for chargeback to infra budget. :white_check_mark:

dan: Final checklist before Tue: (1) publish customer note draft to #customer-success by EOD, (2) confirm opt-outs are excluded from automation, (3) pre-warm eu-west2 spares, (4) patch schedule for host-014 after maintenance. Anyone object?

sre-oncall: I'll be on call during the window and will monitor 5xx/connection reset alerts. If we see sustained degradation >5m, we'll abort and fall back to failover lanes.

dan: Thanks team. I'll post final comms and attach runbook to INFRA-1298. :thumbsup:
